subject: DPA transfer impact & SCCs — review and internal approval runway
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@novonix.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novonix Legal Ops <legal@novonix.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our annotated DPA redlines and a short SCCs mapping our counsel asked me to share. High level asks from Novonix legal:

- Confirmation on controller/processor split and an explicit list of subprocessors and regions of processing.
- A fallback routing option if EU-to-US transfers are restricted (they suggested an export addendum).
- Clarify liability cap carveouts for regulated data types — our legal team is proposing a carveout for regulated medical identifiers.

Please let me know whether Redwood can accept the language in sections 3.1/5.2 as redlined (see Novonix_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). If not, can you propose alternatives and an internal approver who can sign off on the export-routing fallback?

We'd like to keep to the procurement timeline for this quarter — target signature by July 23.

Thanks,
Mateo
Head of Legal Ops
Novonix

Attachments: Novonix_DPA_redline_v1.pdf, SCCs_matrix.xlsx

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@novonix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Mateo — thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Quick responses inline:  

- Controller/processor: Redwood will remain processor for the product in scope. We'll provide the subprocessor list and region mapping (current and planned) — Ben is pulling the latest export.
- Export fallback: we can offer an export addendum with hosting-region constraints as an optional Exhibit B. That will satisfy the routing concern and keep the MSA consistent.
- Liability carveouts: we can't accept unlimited carveouts. For regulated medical identifiers we can agree limited carveouts tied to gross negligence/intentional misconduct language; Laura can advise on specific wording.

Action items:
1) Ben to attach subprocessor + region snapshot and a recommended Exhibit B draft.
2) Laura to propose narrow liability language that can be accepted by both parties.
3) Priya to coordinate a single redline combining Novonix's annotated DPA and Redwood's proposed edits for final legal review.

I'll aim to get the combined redline to you by EOD tomorrow (Fri 07/10). If procurement needs an earlier interim, let me know.

Best,
Priya
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Priya / Laura — attaching the exported subprocessor snapshot and a short Exhibit B draft that implements region-based hosting constraints. Highlights: 

- Current subprocessors: GCP (europe-west1), S3 backups (eu-west-1), Log indexing (eu-central-1). Planned additions shown in SCCs_matrix.xlsx.
- Exhibit B implements per-country routing preference with a pragmatic fallback to EU-hosted staging for emergency processing.
- I included a short ops note about latency/cost tradeoffs if strict region-only routing is enforced.

Laura — for the liability carveout ask, can you propose a short clause that:
1) Lists regulated data categories that may require higher indemnity (we should keep this list tight).
2) Caps Redwood's incremental liability to X times fees for regulated-data incidents and ties to willful misconduct/gross negligence.

I recommend we present a clean combined redline to Novonix that: accepts most of their language in sections 1–2, proposes Redwood counter-language in 3.1/5.2 re: liabilities, and offers Exhibit B as the transfer fallback.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@novonix.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions — proposed liability language and next steps

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the redlines and the quick coordination. I've drafted narrow liability language that I believe is reasonable and should be acceptable to Novonix counsel — attached as a tracked-change snippet in the combined redline (see link below). Key points: 

- Regulated data categories: we accept the proposed definition limited to PII that is subject to EU medical data regulations; we exclude generally defined "customer data" beyond that.
- Cap: Redwood proposes incremental liability for regulated-data incidents capped at 2x the prior 12 months' fees attributable to the account, except in cases of willful misconduct or gross negligence where the cap does not apply.
- Routing fallback: Exhibit B will be optional and only invoked where export restrictions make normal routing infeasible; opt-in by Novonix preserves procurement timelines.

Next steps:
1) Priya — please merge Novonix redlines + Ben's Exhibit B + my liability snippet into a single combined PDF and upload to the shared Drive at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-evidence (accessible to Novonix link).
2) Mateo — ask your counsel for a short call (15–20 min) early next week to agree the Exhibit B approach and fee-attribution mechanics used for the cap.

If you want, I can join the call to expedite wording on the cap.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Legal
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: combined_redline_tracker.pdf (uploaded to Drive), liability_snippet.docx
